title: Papyrus constructs: what Fallout 4 has, and what is a cross-game habit

provenance.note: FO4 Papyrus compiler 2.8.0.4, on this machine, repeated compile cycles. Every negative below was found by compiling, not by reading documentation.
the base script the CK installs is the authority for signatures, read rather than recalled

prose: Every negative here is a genuine the other engine feature, which is exactly why it is tempting. They were each found by compiling against the real FO4 compiler. The practical consequence is structural, not cosmetic: with no array length intrinsic, an editor-filled array is writable in the CK and unreadable at runtime, which is why the facility roster is fifteen named properties. With no CreateObjectAtForm, every reference must exist before it can be placed, which is why every reference is a CK-assigned property. Note exists_in_fo4 is a boolean so a program can branch on it rather than pattern-matching prose.

entries.name: CustomEvent
provenance: probe set VALID: three known-bad controls (event names absent from this build, menu API, Start()) all failed as required, so a pass is a pass
declared in shipped base scripts: ArtilleryReferenceScript.psc:37, BirdSpawnerScript.psc:14, CGNukeFXControlScript.psc:28
entries.consequence: No event injection. Add-ons must poll or monkey-patch. PIP-MON can supply this; see ai_context/the other engine_capability_adoption.md.
entries.replacement: PIP-MON push events, partially declared as RegisterForEvents
entries.note: DECLARATION keyword, no parameters: `customEvent <Name>`. A CustomEvent is declared like a variable. Payload travels in the Var[] passed to SendCustomEvent and is read back by cast. This entry previously said false, and tools/check_item.py was failing four of our own scripts over it -- the obvious 'fix' being to delete working intent. Settled by compiling.

entries.name: Debug script (Debug.Notification, Debug.MessageBox)
entries.evidence: no Debug script exists in FO4 at all
provenance: PROVEN BY COMPILATION 2026-09-30: vprobe/papyrus/probe_papyrus.bat against PapyrusCompiler 2.8.0.4
Data/Scripts/Source/Base/Debug.psc declares: Function Notification(string asNotificationText) native global; Function MessageBox(string asMessageBoxText) native global
called by shipped scripts, e.g. DefaultCaptiveActor.psc:99
entries.consequence: No sanctioned runtime diagnostic channel; mods resort to display hacks.
entries.replacement: PIP-MON wire logging, which is better because it is queryable after a crash and needs no game UI
entries.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-30. This entry claimed false and was failing our own scripts. The call form is Debug.Notification("...") -- dot-qualified, and ALWAYS PARENTHESISED. A bare DebugNotification(...) does not exist; that is the form this entry was probably written about.

entries.name: Menu / Option property types
entries.consequence: No Papyrus-authored menus. INVESTIGATE, not ADOPT: whether FO4 menu internals are reachable natively is unverified.

entries.name: bare Player identifier
entries.consequence: the other enginealike that fails confusingly.

entries.name: array length intrinsic (GetLength)
entries.error_text: not a function or does not exist
entries.consequence: Editor-filled arrays are unreadable at runtime. Structural, not a missing convenience.

entries.name: CreateObjectAtForm
entries.error_text: not a function or does not exist
entries.consequence: No runtime spawn from a FormID, so every reference must pre-exist. This is the 15-property CK assignment tax. PIP-MON can supply it; that is a named ADOPT.

entries.name: Start() / Stop()
entries.error_text: Start is not a function or does not exist
entries.replacement: StartTimer(float afInterval, int aiTimerID) and CancelTimer(int aiTimerID)
entries.consequence: Cosmetic. Rejected as a capability: StartTimer already does the job.

entries.name: OnAddToMenu / OnMenuClick / OnMenuClose in a non-Native script
entries.evidence: compile, plus the toolchain constraint it implies
entries.error_text: these events require the script to be flagged Native
entries.consequence: One script cannot both receive a terminal event and hold state. The two requirements are mutually exclusive in this toolchain, which is why the facility has no in-game menu and OnInit is its only event.
entries.replacement: Split by concern: a Native event shell with no properties that forwards each event onto the wire, and an ordinary script holding state that reads it. Once native-to-Papyrus calls work, the shell can invoke a named function on the state script directly.

entries.name: Event OnTimer(float)
entries.error_text: the parameter types of function ontimer do not match the original script scriptobject
entries.replacement: Event OnTimer(int aiTimerID) - the parameter is the timer ID, not an elapsed time

entries.name: StartTimer
entries.evidence: compile-verified, used by the facility probe
entries.behaviour: Function StartTimer(float afInterval, int aiTimerID = 0) native

entries.name: Native Global functions
entries.behaviour: A Papyrus function may be declared Native only if the containing script is also flagged Native, or every one is rejected at once.

entries.name: data in a Native script
entries.error_text: cannot be defined as native because the script is not flagged as native (inverse case); a Native script may not contain properties or variables
entries.consequence: One script cannot both receive a terminal event and hold state. The two requirements are mutually exclusive in this toolchain, which is why the facility has no in-game menu.

entries.name: property with an initial value, not Auto/AutoReadOnly
entries.error_text: Only Auto and AutoReadOnly properties can have initial values

entries.name: bare ObjectReference property with no initial value
cross-script call with underscore (PipMon_GetVersion)
entries.error_text: not a function or does not exist
entries.consequence: The underscore form is what the VM mangles to, and what the function is called everywhere else in this repository, so this is the single most likely mistake when extending the surface.

entries.name: ObjectReference.PlaceAtMe
entries.behaviour: Returns a NEW Actor, so the result must be cast: akBase.PlaceAtMe(oSpawn, 0, 0) as Actor

entries.name: Actor.EvaluatePackage
entries.behaviour: The reset argument matters. Without it an actor that already ran its package will not pick it up again, so a re-run leaves the previous cast standing still.

entries.name: Event <Script>.<EventName> handler form
provenance: probe set VALID: three known-bad controls (event names absent from this build, menu API, Start()) all failed as required, so a pass is a pass
AOScript.psc:99: Event FollowersScript.Loitering(FollowersScript akSender, Var[] args)
entries.note: THE FO4 RECEIVER PATTERN and the easiest thing to get wrong. There is no OnCustomEvent handler anywhere in the 2,422 shipped base scripts. A receiver declares a handler qualified by the SENDING script's name and reads arguments from the Var[] by cast: args[0] as bool.

detection_note: Entries with exists_in_fo4 false carry a `detect` list of literal stems. tools/artifact_gate.py searches .psc sources for them using word boundaries, so a construct is caught by name rather than by a human remembering it. This is what makes the gate aware of what is passing through it. MenuButton is included with the terminal events because a MenuButton is only usable with them, so flagging it separately would be noise without adding a check.

corrections_2026_09_30.method: Settled by COMPILING against PapyrusCompiler 2.8.0.4, using the build's own 2,422 shipped base scripts as the reference, with three known-bad controls that must fail or the run reports itself invalid.
corrections_2026_09_30.corrected: CustomEvent: exists_in_fo4 false -> TRUE. It compiles.
corrections_2026_09_30.confirmed_correct: SendEvent and RegisterForEvent (names this build does not declare); MenuButton/OnAddToMenu/OnMenuClick/OnMenuClose (no FO4 equivalent); Start()/Stop() (timer API, absent from this build).
corrections_2026_09_30.found_while_probing: The FO4 receiver handler is `Event <SendingScript>.<EventName>(<SendingScript> akSender, Var[] args)`. No OnCustomEvent event exists in this build.
corrections_2026_09_30.papyrus_syntax_notes: Return type goes FIRST: `Bool Function Fire()`, never `Function Fire() as Bool`. The `as` keyword IS valid for CASTS (args[0] as bool). Var[] init uses a single `=`: `Var[] kargs = new Var[2]`, not `:=`.
corrections_2026_09_30.cost: Four of our own scripts were being failed by the wrong entry, and the obvious response was to delete working code.
